frontier.hypothesis: The original C's Case3 arm naturally left a once-assigned local dead at the static-table store — i.e. the construct our Judge reads as a dead store is what the 1997 author actually wrote (a scratch handle set up in the prologue and re-used in the arm), and a rederive/synthesis reconstruction should produce it without being a manufactured coercion.
frontier.mechanism: s7 closes the case analysis: with the in-loop four-way ladder that s3 pinned by instruction count, target's Case3 order is reachable ONLY via combine retargeting the la onto a pseudo whose copy is never read. That is a property of the original's variable usage, not of our spelling — so if target really is pure C, the original had such a variable. The task is to reconstruct WHY, not to manufacture one.
frontier.next_probe: A rederive session should start from the variable inventory rather than the asm: which of the function's values would a PsyQ-era programmer plausibly have kept in a scratch local that is written in the Case3 arm and never read from there (e.g. an offset/handle reused as a temporary), and does that reading survive a fresh adversarial cheat-reviewer as ordinary code rather than a fake? Any reconstruction is one row in tmp/grind/func_80060544/s7/reloc_sweep.py away from a sub-second verdict (gate: launch=1 AND asm_lines == 117), then a sandbox run.

frontier.hypothesis: Do NOT re-probe, on top of the s5/s6 list: loop-peeling the Case3 arm, per-arm or Case3-only address locals, or relocating a staging carrier's other definition.
frontier.mechanism: s7 measured all three dead with mechanism: per-arm/Case3-only locals are loop-invariant and hoisted out of the block by loop.c (+2 insns, launch=0); peeling fires the promotion cleanly but costs five instructions (112 vs 117); downstream relocation of the carrier's definition leaves the copy undeleted (launch=0) and the one relocation that fires costs two instructions on its own. Combined with the s5/s6 do-not-probe list (INSN_PRIORITY, dependence height, ready-list class, LOG_LINKS edges, emission order, statement order, dispatch shape, loop shape, declaration order, carrier type, the call-site cast, and further permuter campaigns), the scheduler-side surface is exhausted.

frontier.mechanism: The complete two-pass case analysis (s6 + s7) is the argument such an escalation would cite: every tiebreak in sched1's ready list is deterministic and favours the a1 set-up; the sole override is adjust_priority's birthing promotion; with target's loop structure held fixed the promotion requires a never-read copy. Exhaustion is the driver's call, not a session's, and the modality ladder still has rederive and synthesis untried.
